messages:
devon: paging oncall — multiple 503s from dedicated cluster for customer Fjord Analytics (eu-west-1). Alert spike started ~10:02 UTC. K/V cache errors and increased tail latency. tagging this as P1 until we know impact. @alex can you take first triage?
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2245 — P1 — service: dedicated-inference-eu-west. Paging @alex. PagerDuty link: https://pd.example/INC-2245
alex: got it. jumping in. seeing elevated 503s on route /v1/stream for model-resolver v2. Rolling back recent kernel tweak? which deploy rolled at 09:55?
devon: deploy-bot shows a runtime kernel patch deployed to eu-west at 09:56 by eng-runtime CI (rev: rt-2024.11). Logs show a handful of kernel ooms around 10:01 then 503 cascade.
li: I'm tailing infra logs. noticed a spike in mem usage on pool-dedicated-03, GC thrash + kernel warnings. kernel patch changed fused-attn buffer alloc path — might be regressing on longer sequences (Fjord runs 4k tokens).
emma: heads-up from CS: Fjord Analytics is on a reserved Dedicated contract (account: fjord-001). Primary contacts: ops@fjord.com, infra-lead@fjord.com. They asked for immediate impact details and ETA. I can send customer comms once we have a clear impact statement.
alex: immediate mitigation: isolating pool-dedicated-03 and migrating active shards to pool-dedicated-05/06. doing canary re-route now. Will also revert kernel tweak on the affected hosts if migrations don't reduce 503s.
incident-bot: ROUTE CHANGE: Traffic reroute requested by alex. Canary shifting 30% -> pool-dedicated-05. Progress: 30% at 10:12 UTC.
devon: -> Emma: here's suggested customer-facing impact line to use in email/portal: "We are investigating increased request failures for models served from your dedicated EU cluster. Some requests may return errors (503) or experience higher latency; we are actively failing over affected nodes and will update within 30 minutes." Thoughts?
emma: good start. Make it explicit for enterprise: include contact routing and workaround: "If you rely on reserved throughput, temporary throttling may occur while we rebalance. For urgent production traffic, reply to this thread to request priority routing to alternative pools." Also add expected next update in 15 minutes.
alex: can confirm canary reduced 503s by ~60% so far. Still seeing intermittent KV cache misses. Rolling kernel revert on pool-dedicated-03 now. revert command: 
```
ansible-playbook -i eu-west-hosts revert-kernel-rt-2024.11.yml --limit pool-dedicated-03
```
Started 10:22 UTC.
li: revert complete on pool-dedicated-03 at 10:28 UTC. tailing logs now. KV cache reclaim looks healthier. Errors dropping to baseline.
incident-bot: UPDATE: Incident INC-2245 status: mitigated -> partial. 503 rate down 92% cluster-wide. Remaining: intermittent high-latency for long sequences.
emma: drafting status page and email. Proposed status page snippet (private to enterprise subscribers):
```
Summary: We experienced elevated request failures (503) for dedicated inference clusters in eu-west affecting a subset of enterprise customers (including Fjord Analytics).
Impact: Some requests may have failed or experienced high latency between 10:02–10:28 UTC. We have successfully remediated the root trigger (runtime kernel change) and rerouted traffic; normal service has resumed for most workloads. Customers running long-sequence jobs may see residual latency until cache warms.
Next steps: Observing for 60 minutes. Follow-up postmortem and rollback details to be shared. If you are a Fjord contact, we will send a tailored notification with exact time window and affected request IDs.
```
emma: customer email draft to Fjord (short):
```
Hi Fjord team — we’re investigating elevated failures for your dedicated EU cluster between ~10:02–10:28 UTC. Root cause: runtime kernel allocation change that triggered mem instability on one pool. Mitigation: we reverted the change and rerouted your traffic; error rates have dropped to baseline. Impact: possible failed requests and higher latency during the window. Next update: 11:00 UTC. If you want an immediate conference call, I can set one up — who should I loop in?
Regards, Emma (CS)
```
devon: add request IDs for their account scope: filter logs for owner:fjord-001 and include 20 exemplar request IDs. Emma, want me to attach those?
emma: please, add 20 request IDs and the pool host list. Also include a brief note about crediting any failed tokens if they want — ops can approve credits.
li: ops ok to approve token credits for confirmed failed requests once CS provides IDs and org. I'll attach authorization to the ticket.
alex: running handoff — I'm heading to meetings at 10:50 UTC. @devon will be primary until I return at 13:00 UTC. Set escalation to oncall-next if regressions spike above 20% error.
devon: ack. I'll monitor and keep triage notes in the incident doc. Current plan: observe 60m, collect logs, prepare postmortem with timeline + mitigation steps + revert checklist.
statusbot: STATUSPAGE DRAFT READY — https://status.redwood.example/incidents/INC-2245-draft (private). Emma please publish once you have the customer-specific request IDs attached.
emma: publishing now to private subscribers and sending tailored email to Fjord ops and infra-lead. Email sent at 10:41 UTC.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: INC-2245 moved to WATCH status at 10:41:45 UTC. Primary assignee: devon.
alex: leaving handoff notes: reverted kernel on pool-dedicated-03, canary reroute completed, error budget unaffected for other tenants. If anything regresses, page PD and @alex.
devon: thanks. closing this thread for active updates — will post final resolution when postmortem is available.
statusbot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (monitoring) — closing notification scheduled in 60 minutes if no regression.
